method: Review completed without a teacher at the owner's request. Rows marked source-verified were checked against the online sources listed. Rows marked reference-pending follow standard grammar references and must pass the automated cross-check (Lexique / Wiktionnaire via the data pipeline) before being promoted. Nothing here is teacher-approved.

rows.notes: Subject pronoun, 1st person singular. Elides to j' before a vowel or mute h.
First part of negation (ne ... pas / jamais / plus / rien / personne). Elides to n'. Often dropped in casual speech, never in careful writing.
Direct, indirect or reflexive object pronoun, 1st person singular. Elides to m'.
Determiner: ce (masc. before consonant), cet (masc. before vowel or mute h), cette (fem.), ces (plural). Pronoun: ce qui, ce que, c'est.
Introduces a subordinate clause. Elides to qu'. Row assumed to be the conjunction sense of the first 'que' entry.
rows.example_fr: Je pense que tu as raison.

rows.notes: Relative pronoun (le livre que j'ai lu), interrogative pronoun (Que veux-tu ?), and ne...que meaning only. Row assumed to be the non-conjunction senses.
Four forms: tout (m.s.), toute (f.s.), tous (m.pl.), toutes (f.pl.). Agrees in gender and number with the noun. Merges the two original adjective rows.

Pronoun: tout va bien; tous/toutes agree in number. Adverb (= entièrement): invariable, EXCEPT before a feminine adjective starting with a consonant or aspirated h, where it agrees: elle est toute contente, elles sont toutes seules, but elle est tout heureuse.
Masculine singular definite article (l' before vowel or mute h; contracts to du, au). Also direct object pronoun (je le vois).
Feminine singular definite article (l' before vowel or mute h). Also direct object pronoun (je la vois).
Interrogative and relative adverb of place or time. The accent separates où from ou (or).
rows.example_fr: Le jour où je suis arrivé.

rows.notes: Only used with il. Present il faut, imperfect il fallait, future il faudra, passé composé il a fallu, subjunctive qu'il faille. Participle fallu never agrees.
Conjunction: si + present usually pairs with a future. Elides only before il and ils (s'il, s'ils), never before elle: si elle vient.
Interrogative and relative pronoun, used after a preposition or on its own: à quoi penses-tu ?, de quoi parles-tu ?
Replaces de + noun. The possessed noun keeps its definite article: l'homme dont la voiture est rouge.
rows.example_en: The book I am talking about.

rows.notes: Interrogative adverb. Standalone Comment ? means 'Pardon?'.
Placed before a statement to form a yes/no question. Elides to est-ce qu' before a vowel.
beau (m.s.), bel (m.s. before vowel or mute h), belle (f.s.), beaux (m.pl.), belles (f.pl.). Usually placed before the noun.
Same form for both genders; plural autres. Before a plural noun with des, des becomes d': d'autres amis.
Possessive determiner before a plural noun: leurs enfants. Also the pronoun les leurs (theirs, plural).

Two roles. (1) Indirect object pronoun, always invariable, placed before a verb: je leur parle (never leurs). (2) Possessive determiner before a singular noun: leur maison. Also le leur / la leur (pronoun).
rows.example_fr: Je leur ai dit de partir.

rows.notes: quel (m.s.), quelle (f.s.), quels (m.pl.), quelles (f.pl.). Interrogative and exclamative.
un (m.), une (f.), des (plural indefinite). Also the numeral one and the pronoun l'un.
